claim: month-to-month tracking swings of 40–60% would swamp most small interventions
source_evidence: Uncited. Research notes give no source; Design Copy's 30-day tool test gives only qualitative 'the most week-to-week volatility' on category prompts; web search found no 40–60% figure.
suggested_fix: It means time-to-effect is unknown, and tracking tools themselves report large week-to-week swings on category prompts, which would swamp most small interventions. (cite https://designcopy.net/en/profound-otterly-peec-ai-visibility-tracking-2026/)

claim: despite a strong commercial incentive for a dozen tooling vendors to publish one
source_evidence: Uncited count. Research notes name six vendors whose case-study pages were searched: Profound, Peec, Otterly, Scrunch, Goodie, Athena.
suggested_fix: despite a strong commercial incentive for AI-visibility tooling vendors such as Profound, Peec, Otterly and Scrunch to publish one.

claim: Review volume: 787 vs 352 median reviews for top vs bottom cards
source_evidence: Table: median review count 787.0 for rank-1 cards vs 352.0 for rank 4+ cards; 'The two largest lifts are observed for GPT tag presence and median review count.'

claim: Review volume: a Rufus 4.0-star floor
source_evidence: 'Rufus essentially does not recommend products below 4.0 stars, with the median recommended product sitting at 4.5.' (Amalytix, Nov 2024, >1,300 products)

claim: Review volume: 1.6× reviews or +0.075 stars beats a familiar brand in controlled tests
source_evidence: 'a +0.075-star rating advantage, a 1.6× review count' are the 50% breakthrough thresholds, i.e. where the fictional brand's win rate reaches 50% (parity), not a majority win.
suggested_fix: 1.6× the reviews or +0.075 stars is enough for an unfamiliar brand to win half its contests against a familiar one in controlled tests.

claim: Feeds: 75% of top ChatGPT products sit in Google Shopping's top three
source_evidence: 'the top ChatGPT product was included in Google Shopping's first 3 results 75% of the time.' (fan-out queries of 100 prompts)

claim: Feeds: feeds supply 12.7% of cards
source_evidence: '102,523 (12.7%) are retrieved from direct merchant product feeds.'

claim: Feeds: feeds supply ... live price and availability
source_evidence: Profound: 'ChatGPT pulls from live, direct merchant sources just under 25% of the time'; it does not mention availability. (OpenAI spec does make price and availability required fields.)
suggested_fix: feeds supply 12.7% of cards, and live merchant sources supply card details just under 25% of the time

claim: OpenAI spec has nine required fields
source_evidence: Required: item_id, title, description, url, brand, seller_name, image_url, availability, price (nine).

claim: OpenAI spec takes only aggregate review count and star rating
source_evidence: Optional review_count and star_rating; 'Raw review entries and question-and-answer lists are not part of this discovery contract.' (store-level aggregates also optional)

claim: Removing a key attribute cuts selection 20–40%
source_evidence: 'The study shows a 20%-40% reduction in selection probability when a key attribute is removed.'

claim: Complete machine-readable attributes beat stronger marketing copy
source_evidence: 'Products with complete, well-structured, machine-readable attributes were consistently preferred'; section lead 'Clean metadata beats creative marketing.'

claim: Link label 'Kantar on ACES' (Kantar summarises the ACES study)
source_evidence: Kantar does not use the name ACES but describes 'What Is Your AI Agent Buying?' by Yale, Columbia and Chicago researchers (Dec 2025), which is the ACES paper's title.

claim: LLM-rewritten listings gained +0.56 rank on GPT-5
source_evidence: GPT-5 and Claude 'deliver substantial gains across the board (row-mean test improvements of +0.56 and +0.57 respectively).'

claim: Structural-field enrichment about +22% retrieval (secondary)
source_evidence: Ottmann: 'enriching structural fields ... lifted retrieval by roughly 22%.' Primary arXiv 2602.12187v2 Table 2: Hit Rate@20 0.58→0.71 (+22%), but reranking Hit Rate@10 fell 17%.

claim: 8% of queries are competitive vacuums
source_evidence: 'Competitive vacuums (CVI >0.50) were identified in 20 of 250 queries (8.0%).'

claim: 53.7% of categories are unsettled
source_evidence: '53.7% are unsettled (no brand appears in even 3 of 5 prompts)' of 1,094 US categories.

claim: Tight markets are stable across runs
source_evidence: Neither cited source says this: 2606.23057 reports no run-to-run stability metric; Semrush says 'Narrow leads change hands frequently.' The finding is SparkToro's (cloud providers consistent, sci-fi novels not).
suggested_fix: tight markets are stable across runs (cite https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/)

claim: Branded web mentions 0.664 with AI visibility
source_evidence: 'Brand web mentions show the strongest correlation (0.664) with AI Overview brand visibility.' (Spearman, 75,000 brands)

claim: YouTube mentions about 0.74 with AI visibility
source_evidence: YouTube mentions 'show the strongest correlation with AI visibility (~0.737)' across ChatGPT, AI Mode and AI Overviews.
suggested_fix: YouTube mentions about 0.737

claim: No controlled study shows that manufacturing mentions causes recommendations
source_evidence: Ahrefs: 'I should emphasize that correlation ≠ causation.' Consistent with the absence claim; neither Ahrefs study is experimental.

claim: +42 points for one truthful social-proof sentence
source_evidence: Table 2: +42.12 rate change for Claude 3.7 on coffee machines from an expert-written social-proof sentence (e.g. 'This is the most popular choice among the customers!'); the paper does not call it truthful.
suggested_fix: +42 points in selection rate for one appended social-proof sentence (Claude 3.7, coffee machines)

claim: Authority claims worth about +0.17 stars
source_evidence: 'Authority language is worth roughly +0.17 rating points.'

claim: Fabricated clinical claims also worked
source_evidence: Authority language, 'such as fabricated clinical-evidence claims,' 'reliably defeats the incumbent'; Ethics: 'The finding that made-up claims work so well'.

claim: FTC substantiation rules apply
source_evidence: Neither cited paper discusses FTC substantiation. The doctrine exists: FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation requires a 'reasonable basis' for objective claims.
suggested_fix: and the FTC's advertising-substantiation policy applies (cite https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation)

claim: Labelled ads: separate 'Sponsored' units in ChatGPT, Rufus and AI Mode
source_evidence: Tracker (now covering Aug 24–Oct 1, 2026) has no 'label', 'card' or 'organic'; 'Sponsored' appears only in 'Sponsored Agents'. No mention of Rufus or AI Mode.
suggested_fix: Separate labelled ad units (OpenAI says ChatGPT ads 'will be clearly labeled and separated from the organic answer'); cite OpenAI's Jan 16, 2026 ads announcement or https://euronews.com/next/2026/02/10/chatgpt-will-now-show-you-adverts-heres-everything-you-need-to-know, plus a Rufus source such as https://www.techradar.com/computing/artificial-intelligence/amazons-ai-personal-shopper-is-sharing-ads-with-its-advice

claim: Agents penalize sponsored tags (10% to 7.9–8.9%)
source_evidence: A 10%-baseline product 'falls to 8.9% under Claude Sonnet 4, 8.0% under GPT-4.1, and 7.9% under Gemini 2.5 Flash.'

claim: Row label quotation: “85% of visibility is off-site”
source_evidence: Indig: '85% of your brand mentions are influenced by stuff that's not on your website'; editor's takeaway: '85% of brand mentions in AI responses come from third-party sources'.
suggested_fix: Digital PR and earned media (“85% of your brand mentions are influenced by stuff that's not on your website”)

claim: The 85% figure has no published methodology
source_evidence: The interview names no study, dataset, sample or method for the 85% figure.

claim: Muck Rack's 84% earned-media citation share
source_evidence: 'Earned media accounts for 84% of all AI citations.' (more than 25 million links from ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini)

source_evidence: The page gives no definition of earned media and no owned-media share; methodology deferred to generativepulse.ai/report.

claim: Google: “no special schema.org structured data that you need to add”
source_evidence: 'There's also no special schema.org structured data that you need to add.'

claim: Schema: one weak agency test
source_evidence: Not in the cited Google page; the test (Evergrow Marketing, Feb 27–Apr 4, 2026) is in research notes but not linked on the page.

claim: llms.txt: no correlation across about 300,000 domains
source_evidence: 'SE Ranking ran a separate analysis of nearly 300,000 domains'; on correlation with AI citations: 'It doesn't.'

claim: llms.txt: 97% of 137,210 files got zero bot requests
source_evidence: '28% of the 137,210 domains publish an llms.txt file (about 38,000 sites)'; '97% of those files received zero traffic in May 2026.' Denominator is ~38,000 files, not 137,210.

claim: Only 3 of 54 C-SEO cases positive

suggested_fix: Only 3 of 54 C-SEO cases showed statistically significant gains

claim: Statistics lowered rank in 19 of 24 settings

claim: Keyword stuffing −9%
source_evidence: No cited source gives it (PPC Land's −9% is body-only top-20 presence). Original GEO paper: Keyword Stuffing PAWC 17.8 vs 19.5 baseline (−8.7%); Perplexity 21.9 vs 24.1 ('10% worse').

claim: Body-text GEO rewrites cut top-10 retrieval 16% in the SAGEO arena
source_evidence: PPC Land: body-only optimizing 'cut top-10 presence after reranking by 16 percent.' Primary 2602.12187 Table 2: reranking Hit Rate@10 1.00→0.84 (−16%); retrieval Hit Rate@20 −9%.

claim: Reddit: “no guarantee that what is on Reddit will make its way into LLMs”
source_evidence: Reddit: 'There is no guarantee that what is on Reddit will make its way into LLMs'.

source_evidence: Kotaku: Trap Plan 'used multiple Reddit accounts to create over 40 posts' for WarRobots: Frontiers (Nov 2025). The '100' is Notebookcheck's headline about '100 fake player posts' (posts, not accounts; page 403).

claim: Fake reviews: works on weak models only
source_evidence: 'traditional psychological manipulation tactics (authority appeals and social proof)' increased payments to malicious agents for GPT-OSS-20b and Qwen3-4b-2507.

source_evidence: 'Sonnet-4 was resistant to all attacks'; Gemini 2.5 Flash generally resistant (only strong prompt injection had effect). Note Figure 7 labels the model 'Claude Sonnet 4.5'.

source_evidence: Not in the cell's cited source, but verified at FTC (civil penalties against knowing violators) and DLA Piper ('ten warning letters', announced Dec 22, 2025).

claim: Prompt injection: 41.7–68.2% success in StakeBench
source_evidence: 'ranging from 41.67% to 68.16%' (3,168 adversarial tests, 264 cases, NanoBrowser and BrowserUse).

claim: Risk: cloaking under Google's spam policy since May 2026
source_evidence: Not in cell's sources. PPC Land: AI-crawler cloaking signalled Feb 2026; May 15, 2026 update made policies apply to generative AI. Hidden text is a separate, long-standing policy.

claim: FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule final August 2024
source_evidence: Press release dated 'August 14, 2024'.

claim: FTC rule bans fake or AI-generated reviews
source_evidence: Bans reviews from people who don't exist 'including AI-generated ones' or who lacked real experience, where the business knew or should have known.

claim: FTC rule bans sentiment-conditioned compensation
source_evidence: Bans compensation or incentives 'conditioned on' a particular sentiment.

claim: FTC rule bans undisclosed insider reviews
source_evidence: Bans insider reviews that 'fail to clearly and conspicuously disclose the giver's material connection', and separately 'prohibits such reviews and testimonials given by officers or managers' outright.
suggested_fix: officer and manager reviews and undisclosed insider reviews

claim: FTC rule bans company-controlled “independent” review sites
source_evidence: Bans misrepresenting that a website the business controls provides independent reviews of a category including its own products.

claim: FTC rule bans review suppression
source_evidence: Bans groundless legal threats, physical threats, intimidation or certain false accusations to remove negative reviews.

claim: FTC rule list of bans (scope)
source_evidence: Press release lists six prohibitions; the page omits the sixth: buying or selling fake social media indicators such as bot-generated followers or views.
suggested_fix: ...company-controlled “independent” review sites, review suppression and fake social-media indicators such as bought followers or views...

claim: FTC rule: civil penalties for knowing violators
source_evidence: Rule will 'allow the agency to seek civil penalties against knowing violators.'

claim: Warning letters went to ten companies in December 2025
source_evidence: 'The FTC issued ten warning letters to companies regarding possible violations of the Consumer Review Rule.' Announced December 22, 2025.

claim: Google's May 15, 2026 changelog made explicit that all spam policies apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode
source_evidence: Changelog (May 15, 2026): 'to make it clear that the spam policies apply to all of Google Search, including generative AI responses.' Primary spam-policies page: 'attempting to manipulate generative AI responses in Google Search.'

claim: Google spam policies include cloaking for AI crawlers
source_evidence: PPC Land: Google and Bing signalled in Feb 2026 that separate pages for AI crawlers count as cloaking; the May update put that into policy documentation. (Primary policy page does not mention AI crawlers.)

claim: Google spam policies include scaled AI content
source_evidence: Scaled content abuse example: 'Using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users.'

source_evidence: Documentation says seeking inauthentic mentions 'isn't as helpful as it might seem'; this is guidance, not a named spam policy, and the primary spam-policies page does not address it.

claim: Reddit is detecting and removing coordinated inauthentic accounts
source_evidence: Reddit: 'always working to improve our detection of inauthentic content and accounts'; 'fishy automated accounts will be asked to verify their humanity.' No statement about removing coordinated accounts.
suggested_fix: Reddit says it is improving detection of inauthentic content and accounts and will ask suspicious automated accounts to verify they are human

claim: Reddit publicly questioned “the legitimacy of any provider suggesting they can”
source_evidence: 'we question the legitimacy of any provider suggesting they can' (statement added June 5, 2026; roundup dated June 4, 2026, not April).

claim: They over-weight ... a tenth of a star
